authoredNote: The FIXTURE FILENAME is the assertion: run as `moved.tf` the document root is `moved`, which is also the address of every block in the file. Names transcribed from a measured run and checked against the source. First transcription put the 2nd/3rd blocks on 15/19; re-read against the numbered source and corrected to 16/21.
rationale: H11 (reviews/hcl/master-review.md) — a defect this lane's own fix introduced, which is why it needed its own fixture rather than a line in an existing one. Emitting a document root (H6) is right: it gives the containment graph a trunk and every non-root symbol an owner, matching the JSON/YAML/SQL/XML convention. But taking the bare file stem collides with any top-level block whose Terraform address equals it, at 308 measured corpus sites, the most frequent being `moved.tf` holding `moved {}` (13 files) and `removed.tf` holding `removed {}` (9). The top-level sibling map is therefore SEEDED with the root name, so the document keeps the bare name and the blocks are disambiguated — and the wrapper nodes (`config_file`, `body`) must PRESERVE that map rather than replacing it, since a wrapper introduces no new sibling level. Both halves were needed: seeding alone fixed nothing until the wrapper descent stopped resetting the map.

forbidRelationships.note: the collision itself: the document and the block sharing one identity, which is also what collapses all three `contains` edges onto one line
